title: The Dead Zone Entry
subtitle: let exists but cannot be touched.
description: Accessing a let variable before its declaration throws — why the TDZ exists.
hints: Hoisting moves the binding, not the value, for every declaration kind.
The temporal dead zone ends exactly at the declaration statement.

solution.summary: The correct answer is D — A ReferenceError is thrown
reasoning: All declarations are hoisted; the difference is initialization.
var starts as undefined; let/const start uninitialized (TDZ).
The TDZ turns read-before-declare into a loud error instead of a silent undefined — a deliberate safety feature.
whyNot: null is printed — No coercion or defaulting applies — the binding is simply not initialized yet.
undefined is printed — That is var behaviour. let bindings are not initialized to undefined; they are uninitialized.
5 is printed — The declaration has not executed yet, so the value does not exist.

learningObjectives: Contrast var, let and const initialization
